content.comment_body: Hi, how can I compare counter values? For example, I want to activate different outputs at various counter values.

Welcome to the forum [user_name]. The up/down counter has an internal comparator, which toggles the digital output. For values from 0 to 32,767, you can use the analog comparator. Do you want to compare values higher than 32,767?
If you need to compare two counters, see the example in the attachment. You can also set one counter to a fixed value without inputs for comparison. Regards, [user_name]

Here is an alternative: recursion works for values over 32,767 with the converters I/F and F/I. I have only tested this in simulation. Be cautious—don't use the VM area of the converters for other applications. The example uses bytes VB0 to VB7 from converters with "double float" type. This recursion might be useful in other cases as well. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are searching for methods to compare counter values in [company_name] devices, mainly to control outputs according to counter thresholds. The discussion highlights the limitations of built-in comparators, which handle values up to 32,767, and more complex solutions utilizing converters for higher values. Suggestions include internal digital/analog comparators and simulation-based mechanisms for large numbers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward way to compare counter values and manage outputs based on those comparisons, including for numbers above 32,767.
